title: Tomato soup with rice and cheese toast
description: Grandma's paradajz juha: smooth tomato soup with a little rice, served with crisp cheese toast.
steps: Chop the onion finely and grate the carrot.
Melt the butter in a pot on medium heat and soften the onion and carrot for 6 minutes.

steps.text: Add the passata, {800 ml} water, the crumbled stock cube and the sugar and bring to a simmer for 10 minutes.
steps.tip: The pinch of sugar takes away the sharpness of the tomatoes.

steps: Add the rice and simmer for 15 minutes more, stirring now and then, until soft. Season with pepper and stir in the chopped parsley.

steps.text: Meanwhile top the bread with sliced cheese and toast it in a dry pan with a lid on, or under the oven grill, until the cheese melts.
steps.tip: Grandma's touch: a spoon of sour cream in each bowl.

title: Broccoli cream soup
description: A smooth, bright green soup of broccoli and potato with a little cream, topped with grated cheese.
steps: Chop the onion and garlic. Peel and dice the potatoes. Cut the broccoli into florets and slice the peeled stalk.
Melt the butter in a pot on medium heat and soften the onion for 5 minutes, then the garlic for a few seconds.

steps.text: Add the potatoes, broccoli, the crumbled stock cube and {1000 ml} water. Simmer for 15 minutes until everything is soft.
steps.tip: Keep a few small florets aside, cooked, to put on top.

steps.text: Blend until smooth with a stick blender, stir in the cream and season with pepper.
steps.tip: Do not boil it long after blending, or the bright green turns dull.

steps: Serve with grated cheese on top and bread.

title: Potato and leek soup with crispy bacon
description: A thick, gentle soup of leeks and potatoes, finished with milk and topped with crisp bacon and spring onion.

steps.text: Slice the leeks into rings and rinse them well in a bowl of water. Chop the onion and dice the potatoes.
steps.tip: Leeks hide soil between the layers. Swish the rings in water and lift them out, so the grit stays behind.

steps: Melt the butter in a pot on medium-low and soften the leeks and onion for 8 minutes without browning.
Add the potatoes, the crumbled stock cube and {900 ml} water and simmer for 20 minutes until the potatoes fall apart.
Meanwhile fry the diced bacon in a dry pan for 6 minutes until crisp.

steps.text: Blend half the soup, or all of it if you like it smooth. Stir in the milk and pepper and heat through without boiling.
steps.tip: Blending only half keeps some texture.

steps: Serve topped with the bacon and sliced spring onion, with bread.

title: Juha od gljiva (mushroom soup)
description: A creamy mushroom soup with dried porcini for depth, finished with sour cream and parsley.
steps: Soak the porcini in {200 ml} hot water for 10 minutes. Slice the mushrooms and chop the onion, garlic and parsley.
Melt the butter in a pot on medium heat and soften the onion for 5 minutes. Turn the heat up, add the mushrooms and fry for 8 minutes until golden.
Stir in the garlic and flour for 1 minute.

steps.text: Chop the porcini and add them with their soaking water (leave the last spoonful with any grit), the crumbled stock cube and {800 ml} water. Simmer for 15 minutes.
steps.tip: The porcini water is full of flavour, so do not pour it away.

steps.text: Mix the sour cream with a ladle of hot soup, then stir it into the pot. Heat through without boiling and season with pepper and parsley.
steps.tip: Mixing the sour cream with hot soup first stops it splitting.

steps: Serve with bread.

title: Grašak (pea stew with chicken)
description: The classic Croatian pea stew with chicken, carrot and potato, thickened with a light roux. Kids love it.
steps: Dice the chicken, carrots and potatoes and chop the onion and parsley.
Heat {1 tbsp} of the oil in a pot on medium and fry the onion and chicken for 6 minutes until the chicken is white all over.
Add the carrots, potatoes, Vegeta and {1000 ml} water and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the peas and simmer for 10 minutes more, until everything is soft.

steps.text: Make the zaprška (roux): heat the rest of the oil in a small pan, stir in the flour for 2 minutes until light golden, then add a ladle of the stew liquid and stir until smooth. Stir it into the pot with the parsley and simmer for 5 minutes.
steps.tip: Taste before adding salt: Vegeta is already salty.

steps.text: Serve with bread.
steps.tip: Grašak is the Croatian school canteen classic. It keeps 3 days.

title: Lentil stew with smoked sausage
description: Leća varivo: brown lentils with carrot, potato and smoked sausage, finished with paprika roux and a splash of vinegar.
steps: Rinse the lentils. Slice the sausage, dice the carrots and potatoes and chop the onion and garlic.
Heat {1 tbsp} of the oil in a large pot on medium and fry the onion and sausage for 5 minutes.

steps.text: Add the lentils, carrots, potatoes, bay leaves, salt and {1600 ml} water. Simmer for 30 minutes until the lentils are soft.
steps.tip: Use brown or green lentils: they hold their shape.

steps.text: Make the zaprška (roux): heat the rest of the oil in a small pan, stir in the flour for 2 minutes until golden, then take it off the heat and stir in the garlic, paprika and tomato paste with a ladle of the stew liquid.
steps.tip: Paprika burns easily, which is why it goes in off the heat.

steps.text: Stir it into the pot and simmer for 5 minutes. Finish with the vinegar.
steps.tip: A splash of vinegar at the end is the Croatian trick that makes lentils taste fresh. The stew keeps 4 days.

title: Chicken korma
description: A mild, creamy curry of chicken with yogurt, ground almonds and gentle spices. A good first curry for children.

steps.text: Start the rice: rinse it, put it in a pot with {550 ml} water and a pinch of salt, bring to the boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 12 minutes. Leave it covered off the heat.
steps.tip: Keeping the lid on is what makes rice fluffy.

steps: Grind the almonds finely in a blender. Chop the onions, grate the garlic and ginger and cut the chicken into bite-size pieces.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large pan on medium-low and soften the onions for 10 minutes without browning.
steps.tip: Korma onions should be soft and sweet, not brown.

steps: Add the garlic, ginger, curry powder and cinnamon and stir for 1 minute. Add the chicken and cook for 5 minutes until white all over.
Stir in the yogurt, almonds, salt and {150 ml} water and simmer gently for 15 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.

steps.text: Stir in the cream and sugar and heat for 2 minutes without boiling. Serve with the rice.
steps.tip: It keeps 3 days. Reheat gently so the sauce stays smooth.

title: Sweet potato and chickpea curry
description: Sweet potato, chickpeas and spinach in a coconut and tomato sauce. Filling, cheap and vegan.

steps.text: Start the rice: rinse it, put it in a pot with {550 ml} water and a pinch of salt, bring to the boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 12 minutes. Leave it covered off the heat.
steps.tip: Keeping the lid on is what makes rice fluffy.

steps: Peel the sweet potatoes and cut them into 2 cm cubes. Chop the onion, grate the garlic and ginger, drain and rinse the chickpeas.
Heat the oil in a large pan on medium and soften the onion for 6 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger and curry powder for 1 minute.

steps.text: Add the sweet potato, tomatoes, coconut milk, chickpeas and salt. Simmer for 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until the sweet potato is soft.
steps.tip: Shake the coconut milk well before opening: the cream separates.

steps: Stir in the spinach until it wilts, squeeze in the lemon juice and serve with the rice.

title: Chicken chow mein
description: Noodles stir-fried with chicken, cabbage, carrot and pepper in a glossy soy and hoisin sauce.
steps: Cook the noodles as the packet says, drain and rinse with cold water. Toss them with the sesame oil so they do not stick.

steps.text: Slice the chicken thinly. Shred the cabbage, cut the carrots and pepper into thin strips, slice the spring onion and grate the garlic and ginger. Mix the soy and hoisin sauce in a cup.
steps.tip: Have everything ready before you start: a stir-fry moves fast.

steps: Heat {1 tbsp} of the sunflower oil in a wok or large frying pan on high and stir-fry the chicken for 5 minutes until golden and cooked through. Lift it out.
Add the rest of the oil and stir-fry the carrot, pepper, cabbage, garlic and ginger for 3 minutes so they stay a little crunchy.

steps.text: Add the noodles, chicken and sauce and toss for 2 minutes until hot and glossy. Scatter with the spring onion.
steps.tip: Lift and toss with two spoons or tongs so the noodles do not break.

title: Peanut noodles with cucumber and egg
description: Noodles in a quick peanut, soy and lime sauce with crunchy cucumber, carrot and a soft egg. Good warm or cold.

steps.text: Boil the eggs for 7 minutes, cool them in cold water and peel.
steps.tip: 7 minutes gives a soft, jammy yolk.

steps: Cook the noodles as the packet says, drain and rinse with cold water.

steps.text: Whisk the peanut butter, soy sauce, honey, lemon juice, grated garlic, chili, sesame oil and about {4 tbsp} hot water into a smooth, pourable sauce.
steps.tip: Add water a spoon at a time: it should coat a spoon but still run.

steps: Cut the cucumber and carrots into thin matchsticks, slice the spring onion and roughly chop the peanuts.
Toss the noodles with the sauce and vegetables. Serve topped with the halved eggs, spring onion and peanuts.

title: Spanish potato tortilla
description: A thick omelette of slowly cooked potatoes and onion, soft in the middle. Lovely warm or cold, with a tomato salad.
steps: Peel the potatoes and slice them thinly. Slice the onion thinly.

steps.text: Heat the olive oil in a non-stick frying pan of about 24 cm on medium-low. Add the potatoes, onion and half the salt, cover and cook for 20 minutes, turning now and then, until soft.
steps.tip: The potatoes should poach gently in the oil, soft and pale, not crisp.

steps: Beat the eggs with the rest of the salt in a large bowl. Lift the potatoes out with a slotted spoon, mix them into the eggs and leave for 5 minutes.
Pour most of the oil out of the pan, leaving a thin layer. Tip in the egg mix, spread it out and cook on medium-low for 6 minutes until the edges are set.

steps.text: Put a large plate over the pan, turn it over quickly, slide the tortilla back in and cook the other side for 4 minutes.
steps.tip: Do it over the sink the first time. A little wobble in the middle is good.

steps.text: Rest for 5 minutes, cut into wedges and serve with sliced tomato, lettuce and bread.
steps.tip: It tastes even better at room temperature and makes a good packed lunch.

title: Chicken caesar wraps
description: Pan-fried chicken, crisp lettuce and parmesan in a light yogurt caesar dressing, rolled in tortillas.
steps: Make the dressing: mix the mayonnaise, yogurt, lemon juice, grated garlic, mustard and half the grated parmesan.

steps.text: Flatten the chicken breasts a little with a pan between baking paper and season with the salt.
steps.tip: Even thickness means juicy chicken that cooks through at the same time.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a frying pan on medium-high and fry the chicken for 5 to 6 minutes on each side until golden and cooked through. Rest it for 3 minutes, then slice.
steps.tip: Leftover roast chicken works perfectly here.

steps: Shred the lettuce and toss it with most of the dressing and the rest of the parmesan.
Warm the tortillas for a few seconds in a dry pan. Fill with lettuce and chicken, add a little more dressing and roll up tightly.

title: Zapečene palačinke (baked cheese crepes)
description: Palačinke rolled around sweet fresh cheese with lemon and raisins, then baked under sour cream until golden. A Zagreb Sunday classic.

steps.text: Whisk the flour, two of the eggs, the salt and a little of the milk into a smooth paste, then whisk in the rest of the milk and {1 tbsp} of the oil. Rest for 10 minutes.
steps.tip: Adding the milk slowly is the trick to a batter without lumps.

steps.text: Heat a frying pan on medium-high, wipe it with oil and fry thin palačinke, about 1 minute on the first side and a few seconds on the second. Stack them on a plate.
steps.tip: The first one is often a bad one. It is the cook's treat.

steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C and oil a baking dish. Mix the cottage cheese with one egg, most of the sugar, the vanilla sugar, grated lemon zest and raisins.
Spread a spoon of filling on each palačinka, roll it up and lay them side by side in the dish.
Whisk the sour cream with the last egg and the rest of the sugar and pour it over the top.

steps.text: Bake for 25 minutes until golden and set. Let it rest for 10 minutes before serving.
steps.tip: Eat warm. Leftovers keep 2 days in the fridge.

title: Sausage, potato and pepper traybake
description: Potatoes roasted with rosemary and paprika, then with peppers, onions and sausages on the same tray. Hardly any washing up.
steps: Heat the oven to 210 °C. Cut the potatoes into chunks, the peppers into strips and the onions into wedges. Crush the garlic cloves.

steps.text: Toss the potatoes on a large tray with the olive oil, salt, rosemary and paprika and roast for 20 minutes.
steps.tip: Spread them out: crowded potatoes steam instead of crisping.

steps.text: Add the peppers, onions, garlic and sausages, turn everything in the oil and roast for 25 minutes more, turning once, until the sausages are browned and the potatoes crisp.
steps.tip: Prick fresh sausages a few times with a fork so they do not burst.

steps: Serve straight from the tray with mustard on the side.
